internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: UNRESOLVED: the Quran-internal evidence has a thing/entity family and a willing/choosing family, but does not itself demonstrate a non-circular bridge between them.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: All 519 confirmed occurrences divide cleanly into 283 noun tokens denoting a thing or particular and 236 verb tokens denoting willing. Both families are internally stable, yet a proposed bridge such as 'a determinate possibility brought into view' merely restates both families at a level too broad to distinguish this root.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Part of speech separates the two dominant families, but form, construction, participants, and context do not supply an internal verse-level bridge from thinghood to willing. No external etymology is admitted to close that gap.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The noun in 10:36 denotes an indefinite thing, while the verb in 10:107 denotes divine willing; neither verse entails the other semantic family.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Thinghood is the primitive and willing selects a thing into realization; the reverse hypothesis makes a thing what can be willed. Both are possible, but neither direction is established internally.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Any bridge broad enough to include every entity and every act of willing also absorbs neighboring creation, choosing, intending, and object-reference language, so distinctiveness fails.
internal_discovery.rationale: Full class-level coverage exposes a real root-unity gap; ambiguity is preserved rather than forced.
